Are our public websites actually ready for the influx of autonomous AI agents?

As developers, we are transitioning rapidly from simple LLM chat interfaces to active agents that run on cloud computers, navigate operating systems, and browse web pages on our behalf. Keeping up with these architectural changes is becoming a daily requirement.

📦 Vercel and Ora have partnered to launch Is Agentic, a free audit tool designed to score public website readiness for AI agents. The tool evaluates websites against 118 specific checks to ensure compatibility with agentic workflows.

🤖 SpaceXAI released Grok Bot, introducing AI agents that run on their own cloud computers. These bots sign into your actual tools, keep working after you close your laptop, and learn how to perform your job by watching you do it just once.

💻 Hands-on developer A/B testing of computer-use capabilities shows ChatGPT significantly outperforming Claude. In real-world tasks like fixing a Windows display glitch or running product searches, Claude reportedly breaks or refuses to act 50% to 70% of the time.

📊 On the data engineering front, new Python workflows are replicating LabPlot's scientific data analysis systems. Developers can now build reusable components to import tabular data, smooth signals, perform Fourier analysis, and execute spectral peak fitting.

This shift means we must design systems that are not just human-friendly, but optimized for machine interaction and continuous background execution.

How are you preparing your web applications and API endpoints for automated agent traffic?
